notes: tier=safe   : pure cache / temp. Deleting costs re-download or a cold start only.
tier=apps   : runtime + model files of AI coding agents. Safe to delete, but the agent re-downloads them on next start.
tier=review : real data (sessions, settings, projects). Never deleted by 'clean'; only ever reported, and only with -Deep.
'keep' lists names that must never be removed even inside a target path (databases, live logs).

targets.label: User TEMP
targets.description: Per-user scratch space. Locked files are skipped automatically.

targets.label: Windows TEMP
targets.description: Machine-wide scratch space. Needs Administrator for the locked subset.

targets.label: Windows Update download cache
targets.description: Already-installed update payloads. Windows re-fetches anything still needed.

targets.label: Delivery Optimization cache
targets.description: Peer-to-peer update chunks. Cleared through the official cmdlet, not by hand.

targets.label: Crash dumps
targets.description: Kernel and user-mode minidumps. Only useful if you are actively debugging a crash.

targets.label: Explorer thumbnail + icon cache
targets.description: Rebuilt on demand. Explorer may hold locks; run 'cguard clean -Admin' for the full clear.

targets.label: $WinREAgent staging
targets.description: Leftovers from a recovery-partition update. Almost always multi-GB and never needed afterwards.

targets.label: OpenCode agent data
targets.description: Shell output, tool output and logs of every OpenCode session. This is the folder that quietly eats tens of GB.

targets.label: Codex runtime cache
targets.description: Downloaded Codex primary runtime. Re-fetched on next launch; ~250 MB each.

targets.label: Codex home (CODEX_HOME)
targets.description: Sessions, skills, config. NOT a cache. Only report it; clean it by hand if you really mean it.

targets.label: Claude Desktop renderer cache
targets.description: Electron Cache/GPUCache/Code Cache only. Conversations and config are untouched.

targets.label: WorkBuddy / CodeBuddy cache
targets.description: Electron caches and rotated logs. Never touches the login state under Local State.

targets.label: Cursor cache
targets.description: Renderer + extension caches. Your chat history lives in state.vscdb and is not touched.

targets.label: VS Code cache (not extensions)
targets.description: Caches and downloaded VSIX installers. Extensions themselves are left alone.

targets.label: VS Code extensions
targets.description: Frequently 1-2 GB. Real functionality, so listing only. Uninstall from inside VS Code.

targets.label: npm cache
targets.description: Content-addressed package cache. 'npm cache verify' would rebuild part of it anyway.

targets.label: npm global install root
targets.description: Installed global CLIs (opencode, codex, ...). Deleting this breaks your tools. Report only.

targets.label: pnpm store
targets.description: Global content store. Safe to prune; pnpm hard-links from it.

targets.label: Yarn cache
targets.description: Offline mirror of downloaded packages.

targets.label: Bun install cache
targets.description: Bun's package cache.

targets.label: uv (Python) cache
targets.description: Wheels and sdists kept by uv.

targets.label: pip cache
targets.description: Downloaded wheels. 'pip cache purge' is the official route.

targets.label: Cargo registry + git cache
targets.description: Rust crate sources and checkouts.

targets.label: Headless browser binaries
targets.description: Puppeteer's Chromium download and Playwright's browser bundles. Re-downloaded on next automation run.

targets.label: Browser HTTP caches
targets.description: Edge and Chrome profile caches. Cookies, history and logins are NOT here.

targets.label: Docker / WSL disk images
targets.description: ext4.vhdx files. These are real disks; shrink them with 'wsl --manage ... --set-sparse' or Docker Desktop, never by deleting.

targets.label: Dell SupportAssist repair snapshots
targets.description: The single biggest offender on Dell machines: SARemediation keeps a full pre-repair image. 48 GB reclaimed here in one run.

targets.label: hiberfil.sys / pagefile.sys
targets.description: Not a folder. Disable hibernation with 'powercfg -h off' if you never use it; that frees RAM-sized GB instantly.
